1.explanation: We import Carbon’s <Search> component and give the input a “name” attribute so that Chrome’s saved entries will appear as an autofill suggestion.  When you accept that suggestion, Chrome applies its default sky-blue autofill styling to the entire field (including the clear button).  Although the component injects an inset WebKitBoxShadow on the <input> itself to reset the background, that box-shadow stops at the input’s border and does not cover the adjacent clear-button element.  That is exactly the scenario shown in your screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: When you use the Carbon React <Search> component in Chrome and you type into the input, Chrome’s built-in autofill (previous entries) turns the input background to its default sky-blue.  The component works around this by applying a huge inset WebKitBoxShadow to the <input> to reset the background, but that only covers the input element itself — it doesn’t cover the adjacent clear button (<button class=“bx--search-close”>).  As a result, the clear (“×”) icon sits on the raw sky-blue autofill background and the white icon becomes low-contrast and hard to see.
